title: Provisioning mini-map and adaptive autoscale cards for Dedicated onboarding
creator: Lina Ortiz
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, developer-oriented set of onboarding visuals for the Dedicated capacity flow that can be used in the quickstart, release notes, and the Console tour. Deliver a 'provisioning mini-map' (a horizontal micro-journey timeline that summarizes setup stages) and a suite of 'adaptive autoscale cards' (config cards that communicate autoscale behavior, cost tradeoffs, and SLA impact).

Scope: 1) Figma files for mini-map with 3 device breakpoints (desktop/tablet/mobile). 2) Four autoscale card variants: conservative, balanced, aggressive, and burst. Each variant includes: title, brief description, predicted throughput (rps), expected tail latency 95/99, estimated monthly token cost range, recommended capacity commit, and visual SLA impact indicator. 3) Two 'SLA heatmap' overlays for the capacity estimator showing region and capacity tier fallbacks. 4) Export-ready PNG/JPEG screenshots for release notes (1200x700 hero, 800x400 inline).

Acceptance criteria: - Figma master file with named components and tokens. - Exported PNGs for hero and inline sizes with no redlines. - Microcopy approved by PM (short hooks and subtle help text). - Accessibility: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary text, keyboard-focus states documented. - Engineering-ready specs: spacing, token sizes, and responsive breakpoint notes included.

Audience: PMs, Developers doing Dedicated onboarding, Solutions engineers and docs writers creating quickstarts.
decisions: Use horizontal 'mini-map' timeline to reduce vertical scroll in the quickstart; each step is a tappable tooltip in mobile.
Autoscale cards will surface three numeric anchors: expected rps, p95 latency, and monthly token cost estimate; use inline info tooltips for methodology.
SLA heatmap overlays will use a 3-tier color ramp (green/amber/red) and a dotted-outline for fallback regions — keeps visual density low while conveying risk.
We will show conservative variant first for new users, with an inline 'Try more aggressive' CTA that expands example throughput and cost deltas.
Follow Redwood token and color design tokens; add an accent stroke when card is selected to match Console visuals.
Accessible color contrast and keyboard focus states are mandatory for release assets.
tradeoffs: Mini-map reduces context for deeply technical users who want full config details on a single page — mitigated by an optional 'advanced settings' link.
Showing cost estimates increases cognitive load but helps set expectations; we keep ranges broad and include a link to a cost explainer modal.
Heatmap simplifies multi-region nuance; engineering may need a separate detailed matrix for large-enterprise configs.
Aggressive visualizations (high throughput) risk encouraging under-provisioning for latency-sensitive workloads; add guardrail copy recommending Dedicated support for critical SLAs.
feedback: PM review (2025-03-14): Liked the conservative-first approach; asked to add an explicit 'SLA at this config' microcopy line under every card.
Eng review (2025-03-16): Asked for precise definitions of rps and latency calc methodology; requested a JSON schema for the autoscale card data (will defer to ENG-1973 for schema work).
Accessibility review (2025-03-18): Color contrast OK for primary text; suggested stronger focus ring for keyboard users.
next_steps: Finalize component tokens and hand off Figma master to Frontend by 2025-03-22.
Create engineering ticket for autoscale card data schema and API hooks (suggested ENG-1973).
Prepare 2-page quickstart screenshot bundle for docs team and update the release notes visuals folder.
Schedule a 30-minute review with Solutions Eng to validate throughput examples (owner: Marco Nguyen).
